mcqs.question: You set `style.width` on 500 elements in a loop and read nothing. How many layout passes does the browser run?
options: 500 — one per style write, since each write changes geometry
500 plus one final pass to reconcile the whole document
Zero — style writes never trigger layout, only reads do
One — the writes mark the tree dirty and layout is deferred to the end of the frame
mcqs.explanation: Writes only set a dirty flag; the browser defers layout until something needs the result, normally just before paint, so 500 writes are absorbed into a single pass. Layout is definitely not zero — the geometry does get recomputed once — it simply happens lazily rather than per write.

mcqs.question: Which of these property accesses will force a synchronous layout when the tree is dirty?
options: `el.getBoundingClientRect()`
`el.className`
`el.dataset.id`
`el.tagName`
mcqs.explanation: `getBoundingClientRect()` returns current geometry, so the browser must resolve any pending layout before it can answer. The others are read straight off the DOM node's own state — class names, data attributes, and tag names carry no geometric information and never trigger layout.

mcqs.question: A loop over 200 cards reads `offsetHeight` and then writes `style.height` on each iteration. Why is this so much slower than the same work reordered?
options: Because writing `style.height` bypasses the CSSOM and re-parses the stylesheet each time
Because reading `offsetHeight` allocates a new layout object per element, exhausting memory
Because the loop runs 200 times instead of the 2 times the batched version runs
Because each write re-dirties layout and the next read must flush it, producing ~199 full layout passes in one task
mcqs.explanation: The alternation is what costs: the write invalidates layout and the following read cannot be answered without recomputing it, so the browser runs a full pass per iteration. The batched version does the identical 200 reads and 200 writes — the iteration count is unchanged, only the number of layout flushes drops.

mcqs.question: A developer moves a thrashing read-write loop inside a `requestAnimationFrame` callback, unchanged. What happens?
options: The thrashing stops, because rAF callbacks run on the compositor thread
It still thrashes — rAF changes when the work runs, not whether reads force layout
The browser automatically batches reads and writes inside rAF callbacks
Layout is skipped entirely, since rAF runs after the frame has already been painted
mcqs.explanation: rAF only schedules the callback just before the next paint; the interleaving inside it still forces a synchronous layout on every read. rAF callbacks run on the main thread, and the browser does no automatic read/write reordering — that separation is the author's job.

mcqs.question: A truncation check that reads `scrollHeight` and writes a class per row is fine at 10 rows but hangs the tab at 2,000. Why is the slowdown worse than 200x?
options: Both the number of forced layout passes and the cost of each pass grow with the list, so they multiply
JavaScript engines deoptimise loops once they exceed a thousand iterations
Class-list writes become progressively slower as the number of CSS rules matched increases
Garbage collection pauses scale with the number of DOM reads performed
mcqs.explanation: More rows mean more forced passes and also a bigger document for each pass to lay out, so the two factors compound into superlinear cost. Engine deoptimisation and GC pauses are real phenomena but neither explains this shape — removing the interleaving alone fixes it completely.

mcqs.question: You need to react when a panel's size changes. Which approach avoids forced synchronous layout?
options: Poll `offsetWidth` on a 100ms `setInterval` and compare with the previous value
Read `getBoundingClientRect()` inside a `resize` event listener on `window`
Use a `ResizeObserver`, which delivers `contentRect` after layout has already run
Read `offsetWidth` at the top of every `requestAnimationFrame` callback
mcqs.explanation: `ResizeObserver` is fired by the engine after layout is computed, so the size arrives without any synchronous pull from your code. Polling and reading in a resize or rAF callback all issue geometry reads that must flush pending layout, and polling additionally does the work even when nothing changed.
